Villacorta: Legal Opinion No. 57 s. 2011 SEP 13 2011 AHO COOIL CENTIALRE ORBS swell' TORE : DATE: TIME: 2 This pertains to your Memorandum requesting our Ieöåi oplnron Hé4äiding the mode of service in the implementation of the decision of the Office of the Ombudsman. In reply thereto, please be informed that since the decision in question was rendered by the Office of the Ombudsman, primarily, the mode of service in the implementation of the Decision shall be governed by the Ombudsman Act and the Ombudsman Rules of Procedure. Considering that the Ombudsman Act and the Ombudsman Rules of Procedure are silent on the matter, the provisions of the Rules of Court shall therefore apply suppletorily. Sections 5 and 6 Rule 13 of the Revised Rules of Court, provides and we quote: "SEC. 5. Mode of Service. — Service of pleadings, motions, notices, orders, judgments and other papers shall be made either personally or by mail. " "SEC. 6. Personal Service. — Service of the papers may be made by delivering personally a copy to the party or his counsel, by leaving it in his office with his clerk or with a person having charge thereof. If no person is found in his office, or his office is not known, or he has no office, then by leaving the copy, between the hours of eight in the morning and six in the evening, at the party's or counsel's residence, if known. with a person of sufficient age and direction then residing therein. " In view of the above-cited provision when the respondent took a leave of absence, the decision of the Ombudsman may be served by leaving the copy of the decision in the office of the respondent with his clerk or with a person having charge thereof. In the event that the Secretary refused to receive the said decision, the same may be served by leaving the copy of the decision in the respondent's office. However, if no person is found in the office of the respondent, the said decision may be served by leaving it between, the hours of eight in the morning and six in the evening at the party's or counsels residence if known, with a person of sufficient age and discretion then residing therein.

-2- Furthermore, if a decision or judgment is not delivered to the respondent for reasons attributable to him, service is deemed completed and the judgment or decision will be considered validly served as long as it can be shown that the attempt to deliver it to her would be valid were it not for his or hMcounseI's refusal to received. [Reyes vs. Comelec, 254 SCRA 5 14]. We hope we have sufficiently addressed your concern. Very truly yours, . JESU . DO Dir tor Ill LS:94/1 1
